source_title: The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power — Season 1 Episode 1 opening witness
continuity_scope: Amazon/Prime Video television continuity only, restricted to the official Prime Video listing and episode synopsis for Season 1 Episode 1, “A Shadow of the Past,” supplemented only by Amazon's official series-identification material. The bounded witness covers Galadriel being disturbed by signs of an ancient evil's return, Arondir making an unsettling discovery, Elrond being presented with a new venture, and Nori breaking the Harfoot community's most deeply held rule. Tolkien's texts, the Jackson films, games, later episodes/seasons, and unofficial rights or lore extrapolations are excluded.

Prime Video official Season 1 listing and episode-one synopsis

coverage_rule: Include every named individual dramatic character in the selected official episode-one synopsis: Galadriel, Arondir, Elrond, and Nori. The ancient evil, Harfoot community, rule, venture, Middle-earth, peoples/species, places, artifacts, orders, magic, titles, languages, ages, histories, and any identity mystery are terms/context rather than character nodes. No name from later episodes, trailers, or wider Season 1 material is added merely because official promotional material mentions it.
omissions: Every named individual absent from the selected episode-one synopsis, including all names introduced by later episodes, trailers, credits outside this witness, and wider Season 1 promotional material.
Tolkien's writings, the Jackson film continuities, games, other adaptations, later Prime Video episodes/seasons, and all non-television or unofficial lore/rights extrapolations.

Peoples/species, ethnicity or cultural coding, places, artifacts, orders, magic systems, titles, languages, age/immortality claims, historical chronology, adaptation-rights interpretations, and identity-resolution claims not stated in the selected episode-one synopsis.
Death, violence, trauma, medical, gender-identity, romance, family, disability, legal, political, or moral claims not directly established by the bounded official text.
Fan wikis, Wikipedia, databases, non-official recaps, social posts, and unlicensed transcripts.
uncertainties: The episode synopsis calls the threat an ancient evil and says Galadriel sees signs of its return. It does not name, identify, embody, explain, or resolve that evil; no later reveal or Tolkien-derived identity is applied.

The synopsis names a Harfoot community and its deeply held rule but does not define the community as a species/race, establish a culture or ethnicity, describe the rule, or state the consequence of Nori breaking it.

The synopsis provides no exact age, lifespan, gender-identity, ethnicity/cultural identity, disability, title, language, artifact, magic system, trauma, violence/death detail, or historical fact for any included character.

Prime Video locates the show thousands of years before Tolkien's The Lord of the Rings, but this is production framing only. It does not authorize importing text, film, adaptation-rights, or future-continuity facts into this television-only pass.
evidence_basis: Official Prime Video and Amazon materials only. Prime Video's episode-one synopsis provides every included name and event claim; its series listing provides the episode title/date and program framing. Amazon series material is used only to establish the Prime Video series identity and to maintain a clear adaptation boundary.
